### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe932dc92d80d4d4f6efaefbb4ed28697e4ecd2b` — the merge of head `1042a83e9e3edb280c82f4ae1995e2abc57bdabf` into base `e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe932dc92d80d4d4f6efaefbb4ed28697e4ecd2b && git checkout fe932dc92d80d4d4f6efaefbb4ed28697e4ecd2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7 1042a83e9e3edb280c82f4ae1995e2abc57bdabf && git checkout -B drift-repro e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7 && git merge --no-ff 1042a83e9e3edb280c82f4ae1995e2abc57bdabf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34686`. No other issue sits next to a closing verb.

**Scope vs claim.** 10 paths. Each is inside the claim as amended, or is listed under the body's "Outside the claimed surface" with the reason a gate required it:
- `scripts/gen-mcp-ask-skill.mjs` (with `--check`) and its output `packages/mcp/src/ask-skill.generated.ts`;
- `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`;
- the new pin `skill-single-source-34686.test.ts` and the updated `mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts`;
- `turbo.json` and `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` (the SKILL.md and generator become test inputs);
- one `GOVERNED_READ_FLOOR` row (`scripts/gen-mcp-ask-skill.mjs` reads `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md`, `declared: false`);
- one changeset.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (the route) is untouched, and `mcp-server-runtime.ts` changes by a doc comment only.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset, and they agree. `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch` is the level `none` takes. The served skill text changes, but no published schema or export does.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34881`: NOT governed, 482 lines.

**Check-runs at 4a78d86b.** 72 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

**Single source.** The generator copies the SKILL.md body after the H1 into `ASK_SKILL_DATA_LOOP` as a joined line array, and `--check` refuses drift. `skill-md.ts` renders it under `## Answering a business question` only when `datasetToolsTaught(options)` holds (dataset tools on, and either `data:read` or no scope list), placed after the data-only block and before `## Conventions & gotchas`. `DATASET_TOOL_LINES` is slimmed to what the skill does not already say. The pin asserts both the generated module and the served section equal the skill body, so an edit to SKILL.md without a regenerate goes red in the MCP suite. The turbo and cross-package inputs make sure that suite re-runs when only SKILL.md changes.

**Console mirror.** `ui/apps/console/.../objectstack-skill.ts` carries no dataset lines, so its default render is unaffected. Nothing to sync there.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. The served skill's step headings land at H2, as siblings of `## Answering a business question` rather than under it. The body chose not to demote them so the copy stays the skill's bytes, and that is a fair trade: the pin is a plain equality, which is the point of the card. If outline nesting ever matters to a client, demoting in the generator and in the pin's extraction rule together keeps the equality. Not owed.
- N2. The dev's open question (should `gen-mcp-ask-skill --check` join a gate family?): I agree with rec A, no. The pin test already fails on drift and re-runs on a SKILL.md-only change through the turbo and cross-package inputs, so a second gate would check the same thing.
- N3. Until #34904 and #34868 land, the served section (from SKILL.md) and the `list_datasets` tool texts describe candidates differently. That window is #34904's to close; I note it there.

Next: o3-E lands. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
